texts.S01:
Statement From NVIDIA Board of Directors | NVIDIA Newsroom

The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.

The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.

While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information.

Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.

The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.
texts.S02:
Nvidia opens probe after report that CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence | RNZ

Nvidia says it is initiating an independent investigation after a media report that founder and CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Top Republican lawmakers in the US House of Representatives have called on Huang to brief Congress this month about a New York Times report in October alleging he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.

The company said on Monday (NZT) that, while its board has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information.

The investigation follows a media report that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of foreign intelligence.

Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added.

Axios reported on Sunday, citing a draft email by Huang to employees, that Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full responsibility for his actions.

"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Huang said in the draft email seen by Reuters.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Axios report.

- Reuters
texts.S03:
整理包／黃仁勳婚外情時間軸：黃樂是誰、川普為何早知情、輝達會換執行長嗎？ | 黃仁勳認外遇 | 全球 | 聯合新聞網
2026-11-09 08:34 聯合報／編譯盧思綸／即時報導

紐約時報報導，輝達執行長黃仁勳8日承認與涉嫌為中國大陸從事間諜活動的女子黃樂有婚外情。輝達董事會已展開調查，若認定他違反公司行為準則，最重可能遭解職。

黃樂是誰？為何接近黃仁勳？
黃仁勳8日在致員工的信中坦承出軌，但未提及女方姓名。根據紐時，這名女子是黃樂（Alice Huang），她是中國大陸公民，曾任Megaspeed高管。
Megaspeed將輝達晶片提供的運算能力出租給阿里巴巴等中國企業，美國官員懷疑，Megaspeed協助將受管制晶片走私至中國。中國大使館稱相關指控是抹黑。
紐時報導，美國情報機構對黃樂進行至少一年的電子監控，認定她與黃仁勳關係密切，並向北京傳遞資訊。美政府高層一份機密備忘錄指，她已被中國國家安全部吸收，任務包括蒐集黃仁勳的資訊，並可能影響輝達，促使公司爭取向中國供應最先進晶片。

婚外情時間軸 台灣淪幽會地點？
2024年6月，台北國際電腦展期間，黃樂在台北一間酒吧與科技業高層聚會。紐時引述在場人士指出，她聲稱能找來黃仁勳，不久他果然穿著招牌黑皮衣現身，與眾人共飲威士忌。
2025年，黃樂據報促成Megaspeed向輝達採購約20億美元GPU。
2025年5月，黃仁勳再度訪台，黃樂也出現在三六食府的商務餐敘。台灣媒體拍到2人搭肩交談、黃樂親吻黃仁勳臉頰；餐後黃仁勳受訪時，黃樂也站在他身後。
2025年5月22日晚間，輝達執行長黃仁勳在台北三六食府宴客，身穿粉紅色無袖洋裝的黃樂（Alice Huang）與黃仁勳搭肩說話。
2026年春天，美國國務卿魯比歐監督起草一份高度機密備忘錄，詳述黃樂受到中國國家安全部吸收、以黃仁勳為目標的情報。這份備忘錄在川普5月訪中前不久，已分送相關安全高層官員。
2026年10月29日，紐時率先披露，美國情報機構認定，與黃仁勳關係密切的黃樂向北京傳遞情報。輝達與黃仁勳當時均稱，雙方往來屬正常客戶互動。
11月7日，金融時報進一步披露，美方情報相信兩人有親密關係。美國眾議員也發函，要求黃仁勳於11月18日出席閉門簡報。
11月8日，黃仁勳發出內部信，承認婚外情並致歉。輝達董事會同日宣布調查，表示沒有理由相信國安或公司機密受損，黃仁勳在調查期間續任執行長。

黃仁勳風暴時間軸
2024年6月：台北電腦展期間的酒吧聚會。黃樂與科技業高層聚會，說能找來黃仁勳；他隨後現身，與眾人喝威士忌。
2025年：據報促成約20億美元GPU採購。Megaspeed向輝達採購約20億美元GPU，據報由黃樂促成。
2025年5月：三六食府商務餐敘。黃仁勳再度訪台，媒體拍到兩人搭肩交談，黃樂親吻他的臉頰。
約2025年底：川普聽取情報簡報。紐約時報報導，川普約一年前已獲簡報，但選擇不採取行動。
2026年春季：魯比歐督導機密備忘錄。備忘錄詳述黃樂被中國國安部吸收、以黃仁勳為目標，在川普5月訪中前不久分送安全高層官員。
2026年11月8日：黃仁勳致信員工承認並道歉。輝達董事會同日宣布調查，稱沒有理由相信國安或公司機密受損，黃仁勳調查期間續任執行長。
2026年11月18日預定：眾議院閉門簡報。3個委員會的共和黨籍主席要求黃仁勳出席。

黃仁勳為何成為中國情報機構的目標？
輝達是AI運算核心晶片GPU的龍頭製造商，對各國發展AI至關重要。美國自2022年起限制向中國出售效能最強的晶片，也讓輝達的出口政策成為美中科技角力的焦點。
黃仁勳對川普的AI與對中政策具有相當影響力。紐時指出，他去年曾說服川普放寬對中國的晶片銷售禁令，兩人後來達成協議，允許輝達向中國出售效能排名第二的晶片，美國政府則抽取25%分成。輝達也已向川普的宴會廳建設基金捐款至少2000萬美元。

川普早就知情？為何沒有採取行動？
紐時報導，川普約一年前已聽取黃仁勳與黃樂相關情報的簡報，但選擇不採取行動。
現任及前任美國官員向紐時表示，川普與黃仁勳的密切關係，阻礙了限制輝達對海外銷售晶片的努力，導致商務部部分調查，以及涉及中國或輝達的貿易制裁提案停滯。

婚外情可能違反輝達哪些規定？
準則適用所有員工與董事會成員，把「私人關係」列為可能產生利益衝突的情況之一。
有利益衝突時，要迴避相關決策並尋求法律指引。
與政府有關聯的人往來要審慎，並思考行為公開後是否站得住腳。
違規可能受到懲處，包括解職。

接下來有哪些調查？目前確認了什麼？
除了輝達董事會的內部調查，美國眾議院3個委員會的共和黨籍主席已要求黃仁勳出席閉門簡報，司法部也已接手聯邦政府對Megaspeed的調查。
黃仁勳目前已承認婚外情，但相關間諜指控仍待調查確認。目前沒有公開證據顯示，他曾向中國情報機構提供公司機密；輝達董事會也表示，沒有理由相信國家安全或公司機密受到損害。

目前誰在查：三條調查各自進行。最近的時間點是11月18日的眾議院閉門簡報。
輝達董事會：內部調查，查黃仁勳是否違反公司行為準則。調查期間黃仁勳續任執行長。
美國眾議院：3個委員會的共和黨籍主席要求黃仁勳出席閉門簡報，預定11月18日。
美國司法部：聯邦政府調查，接手對Megaspeed的調查，焦點是受管制晶片是否流向中國。
texts.S04:
Who Is Alice Huang? US Memo Alleges Jensen Huang Romance With Suspected Spy | Gadgets Now

A Chinese businesswoman who once helped run a Singapore data centre company has put Jensen Huang under a kind of personal scrutiny he has seldom faced in three decades at Nvidia. Two newspapers carried the story in stages. On 29 October 2026 the New York Times wrote that US intelligence agencies regarded Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, as a Chinese intelligence asset who had grown close to Nvidia's chief executive. On 6 November the Times went further, writing that China's Ministry of State Security had recruited her to collect intelligence on him. The same day the Financial Times described a US government memo, drafted earlier this year from intelligence reporting, which claims the two had a romantic relationship. Every one of these claims comes from people briefed on US surveillance, and all remain untested in public. Nvidia calls the business contact ordinary and declined to comment on the memo. China's embassy in Washington calls the spy claims smears. Three Republican committee chairs in the House want Huang in a closed-door briefing on 18 November. This explainer sets out who Alice Huang is, what each newspaper says, and which parts remain unproven.

Who Alice Huang Is, According To US Officials
Alice Huang, who also uses the name Huang Le, is a Chinese citizen and a former senior executive at Megaspeed International. The Singapore company buys Nvidia chips and rents out the computing power. She shares a surname with Jensen Huang, the Taiwan-born co-founder of Nvidia, and the two are unrelated. Her exact title and the date she left remain unclear from public records.

People who have met her describe a fluent English speaker with links to executives across the AI chip trade. The New York Times named Jensen Huang and the leaders of Gigabyte, a Taiwanese firm that assembles Nvidia supercomputers, among her contacts. The newspaper wrote that she attends industry conferences and private executive dinners in Asia. Those contacts sit close to the AI server supply chain that runs through Taiwan.

Her public link to Jensen Huang dates to early June 2024. After a technology trade show in Taipei, she was drinking with AI executives at a bar after midnight, according to an account in the Times. She offered to bring Nvidia's chief to the table. He arrived, and a photograph posted to LinkedIn by a company called NetThunder shows her seated beside him. Megaspeed began a multibillion-dollar purchase of Nvidia's most advanced chips around the same time.

What The New York Times Wrote About The Spy Agency
The first Times story on 29 October said US agencies had kept her under electronic surveillance for at least a year. That surveillance began as an inquiry into suspected chip smuggling, the paper wrote, and it showed how close she had grown to Jensen Huang. President Donald Trump was briefed on the relationship last year and chose to leave the matter alone, according to the Times. The White House has declined to comment on that account.

US officials at that stage believed Jensen Huang was unaware of her intelligence work, the newspaper wrote. The Times also wrote that he had received zero defensive briefing, the warning US agencies sometimes give people targeted by foreign spy services. Huang said in a late-October interview that the US government had kept its suspicions from him. He described his meetings with her as ordinary dealings with a customer.

Its second story on 6 November named the Ministry of State Security, Beijing's main intelligence agency, as the body that recruited her. People briefed on US surveillance said the aim was to learn more about American AI chips. A second aim may have been to steer Nvidia towards lobbying for its most advanced chips to be sold in China. Under present US export rules, Nvidia may sell those chips to Chinese buyers only under licence, if at all.

According to the Times, Alice Huang belonged to a network of companies and investors clustered around Shanghai and Zhejiang province. That network used ties to Shanghai officials to move from mobile video games into data centres. The paper wrote that it also holds an investment in a cybersecurity subsidiary of China Electronics Technology Group, one of China's largest military technology makers. Those business links come from the Times's own reporting and remain untested elsewhere.

What The Financial Times Says The Memo Claims
The claim of a romance between the two comes from a single government document. On 6 November the Financial Times described a US government memo, drafted earlier this year on the basis of intelligence reporting, which claims Jensen Huang and Alice Huang had a romantic relationship. The newspaper attributed its account to people familiar with the memo. GN has had zero access to the memo or the intelligence behind it.

Readers should weigh a claim of this kind with real care. A memo records what officials believed when they wrote it, and its underlying intelligence remains classified. Nvidia declined to comment on the memo and on the assertion of an intimate relationship. The White House and the CIA also declined to comment, and Alice Huang has given zero public response to requests for comment.

Jensen Huang is 63 and has led Nvidia since he co-founded it in 1993. Nvidia has more than once described his dealings with Alice Huang as normal contact with a customer executive, and it insists he shared zero sensitive information with her or anyone else.

Megaspeed, The Singapore Customer At The Centre
Megaspeed was set up in Singapore in 2023 and grew fast into Nvidia's largest buyer in South-East Asia, according to trade press accounts. To many in the industry its sudden, well-funded push into AI came as a surprise, the Times wrote. It bought about US$2 billion of Nvidia's most advanced chips, a figure you should treat as approximate. The company builds data centres in South-East Asia and rents their computing power to customers that include Alibaba, the Chinese internet group.

US officials suspect that rental model handed China a backdoor to restricted Nvidia hardware. The US Commerce Department has examined whether Megaspeed moved chips into China on an unlicensed basis. Singapore police confirmed in October 2025 that they were investigating the company for suspected breaches of domestic law. Both inquiries remain unresolved in public. The status of the US review, including whether it is still open, is unclear.

Nvidia has defended Megaspeed as a customer since the first questions arose in 2025. The company says its own checks found Megaspeed has zero Chinese shareholders and found zero evidence of chips diverted to China. Its statement describes earlier smuggling allegations against Megaspeed as debunked, and it names zero body that carried out that review. Nvidia's statement leaves open whether any regulator has cleared Megaspeed on the record.

How Nvidia, China And Singapore Have Responded
Nvidia: Contact with Alice Huang was routine customer business; declined to comment on the romance memo. 29 October and 6 November 2026.
Jensen Huang: Said in an interview that his dealings concerned Megaspeed as a customer and that Washington kept its suspicions from him. Late October 2026.
Chinese embassy, Washington: Called the claims unsubstantiated smears against China. Late October 2026.
Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs: Said Singapore has run zero investigation of Alice Huang; Megaspeed police case continues. 31 October 2026.
White House and CIA: Declined to comment on the memo. November 2026.
Alice Huang: Gave zero response to requests for comment. To date.

Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs drew a firm line on 31 October. It said Singapore had conducted zero investigation of Alice Huang and rejected any suggestion that its authorities had examined her suspected intelligence links. The separate police case into Megaspeed continues, and police have declined to give details. Singapore has also said it enforces its own laws and applies its own standards to such cases.

Beijing has rejected every part of the account in the plainest terms. The Chinese embassy in Washington called the claims unsubstantiated and described them as smears against China, and the Foreign Ministry in Beijing issued its own denial. The dispute rests on classified material that Washington holds and has kept secret. Beijing tends to answer such claims with denials and counter-charges of American smear campaigns.

Congress Wants Answers On 18 November
Republicans in the House moved within a week of the first story. John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford, who chair three House committees, wrote to Jensen Huang on 5 November asking him to brief them behind closed doors on 18 November. The letter asks about his relationship with Alice Huang and Nvidia's controls over sensitive information. A closed-door session means the public may learn little of what he says.

The three lawmakers wrote that recent stories "raise significant national security concerns regarding the People's Republic of China's access to sensitive US technology and information." Their letter adds that Congress must work out how far US national security has been put at risk. Nvidia has given zero public confirmation of whether Huang will attend.

Timeline Of The Alice Huang Case
2023: Megaspeed founded in Singapore.
Early June 2024: Alice Huang and Jensen Huang photographed together at a Taipei bar after a trade show.
2024: Megaspeed begins a multibillion-dollar purchase of Nvidia chips.
October 2025: Singapore police confirm an investigation into Megaspeed.
2025: President Trump briefed on the relationship, according to The New York Times.
Earlier in 2026: US officials draft memo claiming a romantic relationship, according to the Financial Times.
29 October 2026: The New York Times describes Alice Huang as a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.
31 October 2026: Singapore says it has run zero investigation of Alice Huang.
5 November 2026: Three House committee chairs request a closed-door briefing.
6 November 2026: The New York Times links her to the Ministry of State Security; The Financial Times describes the memo.

Several important facts about the case remain unknown at this stage. Public accounts leave open when Jensen Huang and Alice Huang first met, what the US intelligence behind the memo contains, and whether any information passed from Nvidia to Beijing. Every public claim of spying traces back to unnamed people briefed on surveillance, and both Nvidia and China dispute the central account.
texts.S05:
China denies spy plot targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calls allegations 'smear' | Fox Business

China on Monday rejected allegations of a spying operation targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, dismissing reports of a suspected Chinese intelligence plot as a smear campaign against Beijing.

"The so-called Chinese spy narrative is purely a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters during a regular news briefing in Beijing on Monday.

The denial comes after Nvidia announced an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been the "target of a foreign intelligence effort."

The New York Times previously reported that U.S. intelligence officials determined Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated Chinese business executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed whom U.S. authorities suspect of gathering information for Beijing.

Huang acknowledged an extramarital affair in a letter to Nvidia employees Sunday but did not identify the woman involved. He pledged to cooperate with the company's investigation and emphasized his commitment to U.S. national security.

Beijing has also pushed back against the broader reporting, with some Chinese state media suggesting the allegations were intended to undermine U.S.-China relations.

"Whenever China-US relations begin to improve, there are often those firing shots from the shadows," China's state-owned Global Times wrote.

Nvidia's board has said it has "no reason to believe" that national security or company secrets were compromised.

Reuters contributed to this report.
